title: 2004 AMC 10A 10
statement: Coin \(A\) is flipped three times and coin \(B\) is flipped four times. What is the probability that the number of heads obtained from flipping the two fair coins is the same?

solutions.text:
The two coins match when both show \(0,\) \(1,\) \(2,\) or \(3\) heads. Coin \(A\) has weights \(1, 3, 3, 1\) out of \(8\) and coin \(B\) has weights \(1, 4, 6, 4, 1\) out of \(16.\)

The probability is \[ \begin{aligned} &\dfrac{1\cdot 1 + 3\cdot 4 + 3\cdot 6 + 1\cdot 4}{8 \cdot 16} \\ &= \dfrac{35}{128}. \end{aligned} \]

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: Add up \(P(A = k)\,P(B = k)\) over each possible common count \(k\)
The counts for \(A\) are weighted \(1, 3, 3, 1\) and for \(B\) are \(1, 4, 6, 4, 1\)
